research_question: Under identical evidence, first-record allocation, candidate and refinement opportunities, model, tools and total resources, does typed version/dependency control improve the correct next experiment, selective recheck and fresh-context handoff beyond a strong evidence-aware result tree?

TREE.state: adaptive hypothesis tree containing hypothesis, evidence, failure, insight, artifact and result fields
TREE.policy: Arbor-pinned result-aware tree plus the same raw evidence log and explicit regime facts; result/insight state drives selection but no typed automatic applicability traversal

TYPED.state: the identical adaptive hypothesis tree and raw evidence log
TYPED.policy: the identical Arbor-pinned tree, raw evidence log and regime facts plus typed source/version/validity/applicability/dependency traversal and selective revalidation

falsifiers: TREE matches or exceeds TYPED at equal total cost
TYPED advantage disappears when both receive the same first record and source facts
